sentences.text: Routine mission service begins only after the operational readiness review confirms that ground procedures, staffing rosters, monitoring views, and escalation paths are under configuration control.

The readiness review board verifies that each open action from launch and commissioning has an owner, a due date, and an accepted residual risk statement where closure is not required before service start.
Acceptance evidence is drawn from end-to-end rehearsals, procedure dry runs, interface verification records, capacity tests, security monitoring checks, and operator training completion records.
The Mission Control Center demonstrates continuous console coverage for the agreed service hours and proves that shift handover logs contain the state needed by the incoming controller.
The Flight Dynamics Facility provides readiness evidence showing that orbit products, maneuver screening, and conjunction coordination can be performed within the committed planning cycle.
The Payload Processing Facility demonstrates that science product generation can be sustained during representative contact patterns without manual intervention beyond approved operator actions.
The Network Control System records rehearsal outcomes for planned maintenance, station loss, degraded routing, and restoration of nominal connectivity after a simulated outage.

The Ground Network Manager accepts the antenna readiness baseline only when the North S-Band Antenna, South S-Band Antenna, Kiruna X-Band Antenna, and Svalbard X-Band Antenna have current maintenance clearances.

The Spacecraft Operations Team conducts at least one integrated day-in-the-life rehearsal that includes pass preparation, commanding discipline, telemetry surveillance, anomaly declaration, and recovery reporting.
The Flight Dynamics Team conducts a separate rehearsal for missed tracking data and late orbit update availability to confirm that planning products remain usable under degraded conditions.
The Payload Calibration Team validates that calibration operations are represented in the rehearsal schedule and that product quality decisions can be traced to approved engineering criteria.
The Cybersecurity Desk participates in the final exercise by validating alert routing, privileged access review, and incident coordination with operations management.
The User Services Portal uses the Product Hold List to prevent release of affected products until the applicable hold condition has been cleared.
The Mission Planning System applies the delta note during schedule validation to ensure that contact and activity timing remains consistent with the latest operational constraint.
The Backup Processing Cluster uses the Storage Watermark Snapshot to verify that recovery capacity is sufficient before it accepts routine standby responsibility.
Osprey rejects any command request that lacks the approved authorization state, validation result, and operator acknowledgment required for routine service.
Granite preserves the accepted archive baseline and confirms that retrieval tests meet the service objective before routine operations are declared stable.

Operational key performance indicators include contact success rate, telemetry completeness, command validation timeliness, product latency, product quality disposition time, archive availability, help desk responsiveness, and unresolved anomaly age.
Each key performance indicator has an assigned data source, sampling interval, review owner, threshold, and corrective action trigger so that routine reporting does not depend on informal judgment.
The primary monthly service review compares actual performance against the accepted baseline and records trend explanations for any measure that moves outside the watch band.

The Primary Processing Cluster and Backup Processing Cluster are baselined with approved software versions, processing configurations, capacity reservations, monitoring checks, and rollback instructions before handover.

Configuration baselines for ground software, operational procedures, interface control data, account roles, and monitoring rules are frozen at readiness review entry and changed only through approved change control.

Handover to routine mission service is authorized when acceptance evidence is complete, rehearsals meet their objectives, open risks are acknowledged by accountable owners, and support teams confirm on-call coverage.

After handover, the first operational reporting cycle is treated as a stabilization period in which deviations are reviewed daily and permanent process changes are deferred until sufficient evidence is available.
